pr.title: Add simple async drop glue generation
pr.description:
This is a prototype of the async drop glue generation for some simple types. Async drop glue is intended to behave very similar to the regular drop glue except for being asynchronous. Currently it does not execute synchronous drops but only calls user implementations of `AsyncDrop::async_drop` associative function and awaits the returned future. It is not complete as it only recurses into arrays, slices, tuples, and structs and does not have same sensible restrictions as the old `Drop` trait implementation like having the same bounds as the type definition, while code assumes their existence (requires a future work).

This current design uses a workaround as it does not create any custom async destructor state machine types for ADTs, but instead uses types defined in the std library called future combinators (deferred_async_drop, chain, ready_unit).

Also I recommend reading my [explainer](https://zetanumbers.github.io/book/async-drop-design.html).

This is a part of the [MCP: Low level components for async drop](https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-team/issues/727) work.

Feature completeness:

 - [x] `AsyncDrop` trait
 - [ ] `async_drop_in_place_raw`/async drop glue generation support for
   - [x] Trivially destructible types (integers, bools, floats, string slices, pointers, references, etc.)
   - [x] Arrays and slices (array pointer is unsized into slice pointer)
   - [x] ADTs (enums, structs, unions)
   - [x] tuple-like types (tuples, closures)
   - [ ] Dynamic types (`dyn Trait`, see explainer's [proposed design](https://github.com/zetanumbers/posts/blob/main/async-drop-design.md#async-drop-glue-for-dyn-trait))
   - [ ] coroutines (https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/123948)
 - [x] Async drop glue includes sync drop glue code
 - [x] Cleanup branch generation for `async_drop_in_place_raw`
 - [ ] Union rejects non-trivially async destructible fields
 - [ ] `AsyncDrop` implementation requires same bounds as type definition
 - [ ] Skip trivially destructible fields (optimization)
 - [ ] New [`TyKind::AdtAsyncDestructor`](https://github.com/zetanumbers/posts/blob/main/async-drop-design.md#adt-async-destructor-types) and get rid of combinators
 - [ ] [Synchronously undroppable types](https://github.com/zetanumbers/posts/blob/main/async-drop-design.md#exclusively-async-drop)
 - [ ] Automatic async drop at the end of the scope in async context

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR the Inline pass had a shim-exclusion arm that returned `Ok(())` for `DropGlue`, `CloneShim`, `ThreadLocalShim`, and `FnPtrAddrShim`; `try_instance_mir` special-cased only `DropGlue(_, Some(ty))` when inspecting ADT fields; and `mir_callgraph_reachable` skipped `FnPtrAddrShim` while routing `DropGlue` through a special arm because a not-fully-instantiated drop shim can ICE when its MIR is built. The new `AsyncDropGlueCtorShim` instance kind was not present in any of these paths.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The incorrect transformation is to treat the new `AsyncDropGlueCtorShim` as an ordinary inlinable callee (or omit it from the drop-glue-style cycle arm) instead of routing it with `DropGlue`, so the Inline pass may attempt to build/inline MIR for a not-fully-instantiated shim. A related historical error inside this PR was the inverted no-op test: the intermediate revision used `if ty.is_async_destructor_noop(...)` to choose `AsyncDropGlueCtorShim(def_id, Some(ty))`, which produced Some (nontrivial) for trivially-noop types and None for nontrivial types; the correction is `if !ty.is_async_destructor_noop(...)`. Thus the Inliner could be fed the wrong shim shape and enter its `Some(ty)` ADT-field path for a noop type.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR containing calls to `core::future::async_drop_in_place::<T>` where `T` is a nontrivial async-destructible type (struct, enum, union, array, slice, tuple, closure/coroutine-closure) or a trivially async-destructible type (integer, bool, float, ref, raw pointer, fn item/pointer, never, etc.). The call resolves to `InstanceDef::AsyncDropGlueCtorShim`, with `Some(ty)` for nontrivial shims and `None` for noop shims. The `async_drop` feature is enabled and the Inline MIR pass is run.
analysis.summary: Feature PR adding async drop glue, with Inline-pass guards: `AsyncDropGlueCtorShim` must be excluded from inlining and treated like `DropGlue` during call-graph cycle exploration, and only its `Some(ty)` nontrivial form should receive ADT-field analysis. The PR also fixed its own inverted noop/nontrivial condition. This is reusable pass-correctness knowledge, not a claimed execution or reproduction.
analysis.trigger: The Inline pass considers a callee whose `InstanceDef` is `AsyncDropGlueCtorShim` (from an `async_drop_in_place` call), or `mir_callgraph_reachable` traverses such a shim while deciding whether inlining would create a cycle.
preconditions: The `async_drop` feature is enabled and the source calls `core::future::async_drop_in_place::<T>` (or the std `core::future::async_drop` wrapper) on a supported type.
The callee resolves to `InstanceDef::AsyncDropGlueCtorShim`, which may be either `Some(ty)` (nontrivial) or `None` (noop).
The MIR Inline pass (and its cycle-reachability helper) is running on the caller.
For the ADT-field special case, `try_instance_mir` only matches the `Some(ty)` form; `None` is the noop/trivial shim.
pitfalls: Matching only `AsyncDropGlueCtorShim(_, Some(ty))` in the inliner's exclusion arm lets the `None` noop shim take the normal inlining path; the exclusion arm uses `AsyncDropGlueCtorShim(..)` to cover both.
`try_instance_mir` must not apply its `DropGlue`/ADT field logic to the noop `AsyncDropGlueCtorShim(_, None)` form; only `Some(ty)` is nontrivial.
The noop predicate must be negated when selecting the nontrivial shim: an inverted `is_async_destructor_noop` test swaps `Some`/`None` and can make the Inliner analyze a noop type as an ADT.
Cycle detection must not build MIR for these shims: the source warns that a not fully instantiated drop shim can cause ICEs if one attempts to have its MIR built.
Treating the shim as non-inlinable is separate from the codegen/collector handling of the empty `None` shim; do not conflate the optimization guard with the empty-shim codegen path.
analysis.testStrategy: The patch adds run-pass UI and Miri tests covering async drop of integers, structs, enums, arrays, tuples, closures, references, `ManuallyDrop`, unions, sync `Drop`, async `Drop`, and double-poll idempotency, with expected stdout. It adds no Inline-specific MIR test; the shim builder itself contains `// FIXME: add mir-opt tests`. A focused regression test should compile two otherwise-identical programs differing only in whether the callee is an `AsyncDropGlueCtorShim`, dump MIR (e.g. mir-opt test or `-Zunpretty=mir`), and assert the shim call is not inlined/recursed into and that both `Some(ty)` and `None` resolve correctly. Include a trivial type that should yield `None` and a nontrivial ADT that should yield `Some(ty)`. Do not claim execution or reproduction; no compiler was built here.
